text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia and Russia have good prospects for further developing their economic cooperation, said Russian Ambassador to Yugoslavia Yury Kotov.
- The Independent Serb Democratic Party (SDSS) announces victory in eleven municipalities and two towns in Eastern Slavonia according to unofficial results.

- No major black market cigarette shipment has crossed the Yugoslav border in the past ten days and this has already started affecting street supply and the purchasing price although the street price remains unchanged.
- The long cold weather stretch can delay sowing of sunflower, soybean and corn and affect the growth of crop already sown.

- Firms without a defined owner cannot enter the ownership transformation process and neither can those formed through the separation of former Yugoslav republics until the final division of assets, says ownership transformation minister Milan Beko.
- The draft of the onwnership transformation law expected to be submitted to the Serbian parliament by May 10.
- The first quarter has been characterised by stable prices and production growth and this is a good beginning of the year, says director of federal statistics office Milovan Zivkovic.
- The Serbian parliament expected to pass at its May session laws on ownership transformation, information and concessions, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.

- The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata said she hoped the most favourable solution would be found for some 700,000 refugees in Yugoslavia during her visit to a refugee camp in Sremski Karlovci.
NASA BORBA
- Agreement between Czech Skoda and Serbian power industry Elektroprivreda Srbije for continuation of construction of thermoelectric heating plant Kolubara B is expected to be signed on April 22.
- The London branch of the Banque Nationale de Paris is preparing to offer shares of a large Yugoslav bank to foreign investors, paper learns from London source.
- Yugoslavia owes around $10.5 billion and will have to make concessions to the international community, says Serbian minister for economic and ownership transformation Milan Beko.
- Illegal cigarette sales are twice larger than regular sales the Nis tobacco industry Duvanska Industrija Nis (DIN) said. Monthly black market cigarette sales reach 1,500 tonnes according to DIN.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- EU expected to discuss returning of trade preferentials to Yugoslavia at its April 29 ministerial council session and there are indications the IMF and the World Bank will renew contacts with the National bank of Yugoslavia in the second quarter of this year.
BLIC
- A new meeting on Kosovo to be held in Vienna on April 19-20, not to be attended by ruling Socialist party of Serbia.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- Greek banks ready to grant a $50 million credit to Montenegro for the support of its aluminium and tourism industries and its ecohnomy ministry readu to grant $40 million loan for the purchase of goods. This was arranged during visit of Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic to Athens.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic's office unveiled a letter by Montenegrin state prosecutor Vladimir Susovic regarding abuses of the Montenegrin Security Service which Susovic did not include in a public statement.
- Montenegrin pensioners' association said extraordinary parliament session called for by President Momir Bulatovic might cause tensions and asked for compromise.
- Montenegrin teachers to stage a strike Friday.

- Montenegrin trade unions will organise a protest rally on April 24 in Podgorica over the social situation of workers. If the government does not meet social requests trade unions will organise a general strike and call for early elections.
- Montenegrin power system needs 221 million dinars of investments. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
